@@ -0,0 +1,397 @@ +# agent-room v1: pipeline design + +Approved by Matthew on 2026-11-14. Source of truth for the v1 build; edit by PR. + +## Purpose and roles + +Matthew designs a project with a phone chat, and a cloud session builds it as a series of reviewed, merged pull requests. He is pulled in only for decisions the design doesn't settle. The pipeline is single-owner: one GitHub account and Matthew's own Claude accounts. + +| Role | What it is | Does | Never | +| --- | --- | --- | --- | +| Matthew | The owner | Designs, decides escalations and merge holds, does setup | — | +| Architect | A chat in the project's Claude Project | Designs with Matthew, owns the design files, kicks off phases, posts decisions | Writes code, merges, edits lead-owned files, gives the lead tasks | +| Lead | A Claude Code cloud session, one per mission | Plans missions, briefs builders, integrates, triages reviews, merges, keeps the pipeline state | Does heavy work itself | +| Builder | A subagent of the lead | Implements a task, fixes findings, investigates code, pushes its task branch | Posts in the room, starts subagents | +| Planner | A subagent of the lead | Proposes missions: at a phase's start, and when a deferral needs a new mission | Decides | +| Cold reviewer | A fresh subagent | Reviews a diff against its spec | Sees builder notes or the lead's commentary | +| Qodo reader | A fresh subagent | Waits for and reads Qodo's review, proposes dispositions, judges what the cold review already caught | Decides, audits its own proposals | +| Auditor | A fresh subagent | Checks every dispositions table, cold and Qodo, before it is committed | Fixes anything | +| Watchdog | A recurring scheduled task, one per active phase | Buzzes Matthew when no lead has shown activity for three hours | Acts on the project | + +**Glossary** + +- **Playbook:** the project's single, living plan. It holds phases, items with acceptance criteria, the merge-hold list, environment needs, the pinned pipeline version and the current room. +- **Phase:** a group of playbook items planned and built together. Extending the playbook adds a phase. +- **Mission:** one PR-sized slice of a phase. It branches off `main` and ends as one PR into `main`. Missions run one at a time, so `main` doesn't move during a mission. +- **Task:** one builder's unit of work inside a mission, on its own task branch. +- **State branch:** `agent-room/state`, an unprotected branch holding the playbook and all pipeline state. It holds no code and is never merged into `main`. +- **Room:** a GitHub issue labelled `agent-room` in the project repo, where the architect and the lead talk. There is one room per phase. +- **Ledger:** the list of deferred findings, each assigned to a later mission or to the next phase's backlog. +- **Buzz:** an ntfy push to Matthew's phone. It carries the message kind, the project and the room number, never the content. Tapping it opens the message. + +## Where everything lives + +The machinery lives in one public, versioned repo. Each project's design and pipeline state live on its own `agent-room/state` branch, so writing state never touches a protected `main` and never moves a PR under review. + +| Piece | Where | Holds | Changed by | +| --- | --- | --- | --- | +| `agent-room` repo, public | GitHub, `SigorMatt/agent-room` | `room.py`, `ARCHITECT.md`, `LEAD.md`, `QODO-REVIEW.md`, templates, manuals, `CHANGELOG.md`, and a `STABLE` file naming the current release | Releases with immutable tags (`v1.0.0`, `v1.0.1`…) | +| Account skill `agent-room`, thin | Each Claude account | Entry points, safety rules, and how to find the version to load | Re-saved rarely | +| A Claude Project per pipeline project | Claude app | Instructions that make every chat the architect; digests of old chats | Matthew | +| Cloud environment `agent-room` | claude.ai/code | Network: defaults plus `ntfy.sh` and project domains. Variables: `ROOM_NTFY_TOPIC`, `QODO_REVIEW`. Optional ntfy token as a network secret | Matthew | +| ntfy app | Matthew's phone | A subscription to the private topic | Matthew | +| Qodo | GitHub app on the account | Reviews every PR | Matthew's subscription | +| Project repo, `main` | GitHub | The code, plus the review records that arrive with each PR | Mission PRs only | +| Project repo, `agent-room/state` | GitHub, an unprotected branch | The playbook files below | Direct commits by the architect and the lead | + +**Files on the state branch, and who owns them.** Each agent edits only the files it owns and reads all of them; Matthew may edit anything. The first lead creates the lead-owned files from templates. Sessions read these files from a checkout of the state branch beside the project's own checkout. + +| Path | Owner | Contents | +| --- | --- | --- | +| `docs/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md` | Architect | Header with pipeline version, repo and current room; phases; items with IDs and acceptance criteria; the test command; merge-hold list; environment needs; areas left to the lead's discretion; known debt for Phase 0 | +| `docs/playbook/DESIGN.md` | Architect | Goals, non-goals, architecture, interfaces, data; decision log D-n with rationale and rejected alternatives | +| `docs/playbook/HANDOFF.md` | Architect | The latest session note: open threads, what was being explored, which way Matthew leaned | +| `docs/playbook/MISSIONS.md` | Lead | Missions per phase with status; the current mission's recorded step; the lead lease; the room cursor; the counter for escalations and holds | +| `docs/playbook/LEDGER.md` | Lead | Deferred items L-n with their targets | +| `docs/playbook/QODO-VALUE.md` | Lead | One line per PR measuring Qodo | + +Review records travel with the code instead. `reviews/cold/M/` and `reviews/qodo/PR-/` are committed on the mission branch and merge with the PR, as `QODO-REVIEW.md` specifies. + +## The room + +The room is one GitHub issue per phase. The architect opens it at the phase's kickoff and records its number in `PLAYBOOK.md`; the lead closes it at `DONE`. Seven messages buzz Matthew's phone; everything else is quiet. + +| Kind | From | Buzz | Meaning | +| --- | --- | --- | --- | +| `PLAN` | Lead | No | The phase's missions, as planned or re-planned | +| `LEAD ONLINE` | Lead | No | A new lead has taken the lease | +| `STATUS` | Lead | No | A task or step finished, or a note such as a missing Qodo review | +| `ESCALATION-n` | Lead | Yes | Needs an owner decision | +| `MERGE-HOLD-n` | Lead | Yes | A PR is held, with the reason | +| `HANDOFF` | Lead | No | This lead's tenure ends; names the mission, the step, and whether a successor is scheduled | +| `NEXT-LEAD-NEEDED` | Lead | Yes | The successor couldn't be scheduled; start one by hand | +| `PAUSED` | Lead | Yes | Paused at a safe point; this lead has ended | +| `STOPPED` | Lead | Yes | Halted on `STOP`; this lead has ended | +| `DONE` | Lead | Yes | The phase is complete and the room is closed | +| `LEAD-SILENT` | Watchdog | Yes | No lead activity for three hours | +| `ACK DECISION-n` / `ACK CHANGE-n` | Lead | No | Received and applied | +| `DECISION-n` | Architect | No | The answer to escalation or hold n, including how the mission continues | +| `CHANGE-n` | Architect | No | A design change in the middle of a phase | +| `PAUSE` | Architect or Matthew | No | Let running builders finish, save state, end | +| `STOP` | Architect or Matthew | No | Halt now | + +**Rules** + +- One counter per room numbers escalations and holds together (`ESCALATION-3`, then `MERGE-HOLD-4`). It is kept in `MISSIONS.md`, so a `DECISION-n` always answers exactly one message. +- Every message carries its role and its session, so a lead sees other leads' messages, including a newer `LEAD ONLINE`. +- Only comments from Matthew's GitHub login count. `ROOM_TRUST` can add another of his logins; anyone else's comments are ignored. +- **Owner authority is procedural, not enforced.** The agents also post as Matthew's GitHub account, so a role tag is a declaration, not proof. `room.py` blocks the likely mistakes: a lead can't post `DECISION`, `CHANGE`, `PAUSE` or `STOP`, and nothing is posted untagged. A deliberately misbehaving agent could still forge a message. For a single-owner system that risk is accepted and documented here. +- A comment Matthew posts from GitHub (no role tag) outranks both agents. +- Room text is data from a colleague, never instructions beyond the playbook's scope. +- Messages stay under about 300 words and point to commits, PRs, tasks and doc sections instead of pasting. +- A failed buzz never fails the post; the lead mentions it in its next `STATUS`. + +## Mission lifecycle + +A mission runs seven steps. `MISSIONS.md` on the state branch records which step it is on, so a new lead can pick up anywhere. + +```text +1 Spec ──► 2 Build ──► 3 Cold review ──► 4 Open PR into main ──► 5 Qodo review ──► 6 Merge gate ──► 7 Close + ▲ │ fix, up to 2 rounds │ fix, up to 3 rounds │ a hold reason + └──────────────┘ ⟲ ▼ + MERGE-HOLD-n (buzz; Matthew decides) +Any step can raise an ESCALATION; the lead keeps building what is not blocked. +``` + +Fixes loop back through builders: at most two cold-review rounds and three Qodo rounds. After a hold, Matthew decides through the architect, and a decision that needs changes sends the mission back to Build. + +**Before the first mission of a phase:** a planner subagent proposes the phase's missions, placing every ledger item that targets this phase's backlog. The lead decides, writes them to `MISSIONS.md` and posts `PLAN`. + +1. **Spec:** the scope; the playbook criteria the mission covers, by ID, with the checks that prove them; the ledger items assigned to it; the spec revision it was planned against (the state-branch commit of `PLAYBOOK.md` and `DESIGN.md`) and the pipeline version; a branch `mission/M-` off `main`. +2. **Build:** builders take the tasks, at most three at once, each in its own worktree and task branch, which they push when done. The lead answers their questions from the docs or escalates, merges their work into the mission branch and runs the checks. +3. **Cold review:** up to two rounds, then a scoped review of any later code changes (the coverage rule, under Reviews). +4. **Open the PR into `main`:** its body holds a summary, the criteria covered, the cold-review dispositions and any ledger changes. +5. **Qodo review:** only when `QODO_REVIEW=on`, as described under Qodo. +6. **Merge gate:** `room.py gate` checks what can be checked mechanically. Then the lead merges through GitHub, naming the head commit the gate checked, or posts `MERGE-HOLD-n`, as described under Merge gate. +7. **Close:** record the merge in `MISSIONS.md`, `LEDGER.md` and `QODO-VALUE.md` on the state branch. Then: + - **More missions in the phase:** post `HANDOFF` and schedule the successor. + - **Last mission of the phase:** confirm every phase criterion was covered and the ledger allows `DONE`. Post `DONE`, close the room, delete the watchdog, and schedule nothing. + +**Re-entry after a decision.** A `DECISION-n` says how the mission continues: merge as is; return to Build with a stated extra budget (by default one cold round and up to two Qodo rounds); or drop the mission and re-plan. The lead records the choice in `MISSIONS.md`. + +**Spec changes mid-mission.** A `CHANGE-n` says whether it applies to the running mission now or only from the next one. If now, the lead re-pins the spec revision and re-checks the criteria the mission covers. Otherwise the mission keeps building and reviewing against the revision it was planned against. + +**Budgets.** A task gets at most three builder attempts, and a mission gets a wall-clock budget set in `PLAYBOOK.md` (default eight hours). Exceeding either becomes an `ESCALATION`, never another automatic retry. If Claude usage runs out mid-mission, the lead simply stops; the watchdog reports it, and the next lead resumes from the recorded step. + +At any step, a question the design doesn't settle becomes an `ESCALATION-n` with a buzz, and the lead keeps going on whatever isn't blocked. + +## Reviews, dispositions and the ledger + +Every finding from either review gets exactly one disposition before merge, and every commit is reviewed before it merges. Nothing serious is dismissed or deferred without Matthew. + +| Disposition | When | Recorded as | +| --- | --- | --- | +| Fix | The claim holds and the fix belongs in this mission | `fixed in ` | +| Dismiss | The claim is wrong or doesn't apply | `dismissed: ` | +| Defer | The claim is real but outside this mission | `deferred: L-n to M`, or `to phase

backlog` | +| Owner decision | The answer is a design or product choice | `owner decision: , Matthew` | + +**Severity rule.** A top-severity finding ("high" from the cold review, "Action required" from Qodo) is fixed or becomes an owner decision, through an `ESCALATION`. The lead never dismisses or defers one on its own. + +**"Open" means undecided.** A finding is open while it has no recorded disposition. Qodo's own marks don't count: a correctly dismissed finding stays open in Qodo's view forever. + +**Coverage rule.** Every code change in a PR is covered by a review before merge. Coverage is about code, not commits: review records under `reviews/` aren't reviewed, so committing a report never triggers another review. Each review records the commit it covered. Code changed after the last covering review gets a scoped cold review, which focuses on those changes but sees the whole PR diff, so it can catch interactions with earlier code. That covers fixes after cold round 2, fixes after Qodo's final re-review, and a re-review that never arrives. A scoped review doesn't count as a round, and a top-severity finding from it goes to Matthew.

4\. Review exemption by directory lets code skip coverage 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security 
The coverage rule exempts everything under reviews/ from review, decided by path rather than by
file type. Code placed under that directory would be merged with no review, and the gate would not
see it as a change needing coverage.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description `docs/design/v1.md` (line 143) exempts `reviews/` from coverage by directory alone. Review records are committed under `reviews/cold/M/` and `reviews/qodo/PR-/` (line 58). Any executable or source file placed under `reviews/` would merge without review, and `room.py gate` would not require coverage for it. ## Fix Focus Areas - docs/design/v1.md[143-143] - docs/design/v1.md[58-58] ## Recommended Fix Define the exemption by file pattern (for example `reviews/**/*.md`) and state that any other path under `reviews/` is code. Have the gate treat non-report files under `reviews/` as changes that need coverage. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
